stated: Reform UK will implement zero-tolerance policing, clamping down on all crime and antisocial behaviour, substantially increasing Stop and Search, mandating prison for violent crimes and knife possession, and imposing mandatory life imprisonment for drug dealing and trafficking. A new offence of Substantial Possession of Drugs will carry heavy fines.

source.quote: Commence Zero Tolerance Policing Clampdown on all crime and antisocial behaviour. Increase Stop and Search substantially. Prison for violent crimes and possessing a knife. Drug dealing and trafficking will get mandatory life imprisonment. A new offence of Substantial Possession of Drugs will meet heavy fines.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses crime rates, antisocial behaviour, policing powers (stop and search), and the justice system (mandatory sentencing for violence, knife possession, and drug offences) — the core of O5's scope.

Substantially increasing Stop and Search is a concrete mechanism with documented racial disproportionality in UK data, directly affecting equal treatment / anti-discrimination protections — a specific O9 indicator.

Substantially increasing Stop and Search, creating a new criminal offence (Substantial Possession of Drugs), and imposing mandatory/life sentences materially expand state coercive power over individuals' bodies and choices — a concrete worsening mechanism for personal liberty.

Mandatory life imprisonment for drug dealing and trafficking — a broad offence category — would dramatically increase the prison population and require major additional capacity spending, creating a material and specific fiscal burden on public finances.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: the policy's safety intent (O5), the liberty cost of expanded coercion/surveillance (O10), the equal-treatment risk from disproportionate Stop and Search (O9), and the fiscal cost of mandatory-life sentencing driving prison population growth (O12). No other fundamentals are non-negligibly affected by the specific mechanisms described.
